d2=4d_2 = 4d2​=4 cm

questions.question_text: In a 3-digit number N, the digits are non-zero and distinct such that none of the digits is a perfect square, and only one of the digits is a prime number. Then, the number of factors of the minimum possible value of N is
questions.explanation_text:
The digits are non-zero, so the available digits are 111 through 999.

Removing perfect squares (1,4,91, 4, 91,4,9), the allowed digits are: 2,3,5,6,7,82, 3, 5, 6, 7, 82,3,5,6,7,8

Among these:

  • Prime digits: 2,3,5,72, 3, 5, 72,3,5,7
  • Non-prime digits: 6,86, 86,8

Since exactly one digit must be prime, the other two digits must be non-prime.

The only non-prime allowed digits are 666 and 888, so these two must be used.

The third digit (the prime one) can be: 2,3,5,2, 3, 5,2,3,5, or 777

To minimize NNN, the hundreds digit should be as small as possible.

The smallest available prime is 222, so the digits are {2,6,8}\{2, 6, 8\}{2,6,8}.

Arranging in ascending order to get the smallest 3-digit number:

Nmin⁡=268N_{\min} = 268Nmin​=268

Prime factorisation of 268268268:

268=2×134268 = 2 \times 134268=2×134

=2×2×67= 2 \times 2 \times 67=2×2×67

=22×67= 2^2 \times 67=22×67

Here, 676767 is prime since it is not divisible by 2,3,5,2, 3, 5,2,3,5, or 777.

If N=pa×qbN = p^a \times q^bN=pa×qb, then number of factors =(a+1)(b+1)= (a+1)(b+1)=(a+1)(b+1)

Number of factors of 268268268

=(2+1)(1+1)= (2+1)(1+1)=(2+1)(1+1)

=3×2= 3 \times 2=3×2

=6= 6=6

Since adding sauces is optional, all three cases need to be considered:

Total sauce options =1+6+15=22= 1 + 6 + 15 = 22=1+6+15=22 ways

Since all 4 choices are independent of each other, the total number of ways to place an order:

=5×4×2×22= 5 \times 4 \times 2 \times 22=5×4×2×22

=40×22= 40 \times 22=40×22

=880= 880=880

questions.question_text: If the length of a side of a rhombus is 36 cm and the area of the rhombus is 396 sq. cm, then the absolute value of the difference between the lengths, in cm, of the diagonals of the rhombus is
questions.explanation_text:
Let d1d_1d1​ and d2d_2d2​ be the two diagonals of the rhombus.

The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at 90 degrees, so each side forms a right triangle with half-diagonals:

side2=(d12)2+(d22)2\text{side}^2 = \left(\dfrac{d_1}{2}\right)^2 + \left(\dfrac{d_2}{2}\right)^2side2=(2d1​​)2+(2d2​​)2

12×d1×d2=396\dfrac{1}{2} \times d_1 \times d_2 = 39621​×d1​×d2​=396

362=d124+d22436^2 = \dfrac{d_1^2}{4} + \dfrac{d_2^2}{4}362=4d12​​+4d22​​

1296=d12+d2241296 = \dfrac{d_1^2 + d_2^2}{4}1296=4d12​+d22​​

d12+d22=5184...(ii)d_1^2 + d_2^2 = 5184 \quad \text{...(ii)}d12​+d22​=5184...(ii)

Using the identity (d1−d2)2=(d12+d22)−2(d1⋅d2)(d_1 - d_2)^2 = (d_1^2 + d_2^2) - 2(d_1 \cdot d_2)(d1​−d2​)2=(d12​+d22​)−2(d1​⋅d2​) with (i) and (ii):

(d1−d2)2=5184−2(792)(d_1 - d_2)^2 = 5184 - 2(792)(d1​−d2​)2=5184−2(792)

questions.question_text: Shruti travels a distance of 224 km in four parts for a total travel time of 3 hours. Her speeds in these four parts follow an arithmetic progression, and the corresponding time taken to cover these four parts follow another arithmetic progression. If she travels at a speed of 960 meters per minute for 30 minutes to cover the first part, then the distance, in meters, she travels in the fourth part is
questions.explanation_text:
Converting units to meters and minutes:

Total distance =224 km=224,000 m= 224 \text{ km} = 224,000 \text{ m}=224 km=224,000 m

Total time =3 hours=180 minutes= 3 \text{ hours} = 180 \text{ minutes}=3 hours=180 minutes

First part: speed =960 m/min= 960 \text{ m/min}=960 m/min, time =30 min= 30 \text{ min}=30 min

Let the four times be t1,t2,t3,t4t_1, t_2, t_3, t_4t1​,t2​,t3​,t4​ in AP, with t1=30t_1 = 30t1​=30 min.

Sum of all four times =180= 180=180 min

Average time =1804=45= \dfrac{180}{4} = 45=4180​=45 min

In an AP, the average of all terms equals the average of the first and last terms:

t1+t42=45\dfrac{t_1 + t_4}{2} = 452t1​+t4​​=45

30+t42=45\dfrac{30 + t_4}{2} = 45230+t4​​=45

t4=60t_4 = 60t4​=60 min

Common difference =60−303=10= \dfrac{60 - 30}{3} = 10=360−30​=10 min

So the four times are: 30,40,50,6030, 40, 50, 6030,40,50,60 minutes.

Let the four speeds be 960,960+d,960+2d,960+3d960, 960+d, 960+2d, 960+3d960,960+d,960+2d,960+3d (in m/min).

Since Distance === Speed ×\times× Time, the four distances are:

Part 1: 960×30=28,800960 \times 30 = 28,800960×30=28,800

Part 2: (960+d)×40=38,400+40d(960 + d) \times 40 = 38,400 + 40d(960+d)×40=38,400+40d

Part 3: (960+2d)×50=48,000+100d(960 + 2d) \times 50 = 48,000 + 100d(960+2d)×50=48,000+100d

Part 4: (960+3d)×60=57,600+180d(960 + 3d) \times 60 = 57,600 + 180d(960+3d)×60=57,600+180d

Adding all four distances and setting equal to 224,000224,000224,000:

28,800+38,400+48,000+57,600+(40+100+180)d=224,00028,800 + 38,400 + 48,000 + 57,600 + (40 + 100 + 180)d = 224,00028,800+38,400+48,000+57,600+(40+100+180)d=224,000

172,800+320d=224,000172,800 + 320d = 224,000172,800+320d=224,000

320d=51,200320d = 51,200320d=51,200

d=160d = 160d=160

Speed in the 4th part =960+3(160)=1,440= 960 + 3(160) = 1,440=960+3(160)=1,440 m/min

Time in the 4th part =60= 60=60 min

Distance in the 4th part =1,440×60=86,400= 1,440 \times 60 = 86,400=1,440×60=86,400 meters

questions.question_text: A container holds 200 litres of a solution of acid and water, having 30% acid by volume. Atul replaces 20% of this solution with water, then replaces 10% of the resulting solution with acid, and finally replaces 15% of the solution thus obtained, with water. The percentage of acid by volume in the final solution obtained after these three replacements, is nearest to
questions.explanation_text:
Initial solution: 200 L with 30% acid

Acid =60= 60=60 L, Water =140= 140=140 L

Since the same quantity is always added back after removal, the total volume stays at 200 L throughout. Only the acid percentage needs to be tracked.

When replacing x%x\%x% of the solution with water, the new acid % === old acid % ×(1−x100)\times \left(1 - \dfrac{x}{100}\right)×(1−100x​)

When replacing x%x\%x% of the solution with acid, the new acid % === old acid % ×(1−x100)+x%\times \left(1 - \dfrac{x}{100}\right) + x\%×(1−100x​)+x%

Replacing 20% of the solution with water:

Acid % =30%×(1−0.20)= 30\% \times (1 - 0.20)=30%×(1−0.20)

=30%×0.80= 30\% \times 0.80=30%×0.80

=24%= 24\%=24%

Replacing 10% of the resulting solution with acid:

Acid % =24%×(1−0.10)+10%= 24\% \times (1 - 0.10) + 10\%=24%×(1−0.10)+10%

=24%×0.90+10%= 24\% \times 0.90 + 10\%=24%×0.90+10%

=21.6%+10%= 21.6\% + 10\%=21.6%+10%

=31.6%= 31.6\%=31.6%

Replacing 15% of the resulting solution with water:

Acid % =31.6%×(1−0.15)= 31.6\% \times (1 - 0.15)=31.6%×(1−0.15)

=31.6%×0.85= 31.6\% \times 0.85=31.6%×0.85

=26.86%= 26.86\%=26.86%

26.86%≈27%26.86\% \approx 27\%26.86%≈27%

The percentage of acid by volume in the final solution is nearest to 27%.

questions.question_text: Arun, Varun and Tarun, if working alone, can complete a task in 24, 21, and 15 days, respectively. They charge Rs 2160, Rs 2400, and Rs 2160 per day, respectively, even if they are employed for a partial day. On any given day, any of the workers may or may not be employed to work. If the task needs to be completed in 10 days or less, then the minimum possible amount, in rupees, required to be paid for the entire task is
questions.explanation_text:
Work done per day by each worker:

Arun =124= \dfrac{1}{24}=241​

Varun =121= \dfrac{1}{21}=211​

Tarun =115= \dfrac{1}{15}=151​

To minimize cost, find the cost each worker would charge to complete the entire task alone:

Arun =2160×24== 2160 \times 24 = =2160×24= Rs 51,84051,84051,840

Varun =2400×21== 2400 \times 21 = =2400×21= Rs 50,40050,40050,400

Tarun =2160×15== 2160 \times 15 = =2160×15= Rs 32,40032,40032,400

So Tarun is the cheapest per unit of work, followed by Varun, then Arun.

To minimize cost, employ Tarun for the maximum allowed 10 days:

Work done by Tarun in 10 days =1015=23= \dfrac{10}{15} = \dfrac{2}{3}=1510​=32​

Remaining work =1−23=13= 1 - \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{1}{3}=1−32​=31​

The next cheapest worker is Varun. Days Varun needs for the remaining 13\dfrac{1}{3}31​ work:

=1/31/21= \dfrac{1/3}{1/21}=1/211/3​

=213= \dfrac{21}{3}=321​

=7= 7=7 days

This is within the 10-day limit, since Varun works alongside Tarun on 7 of those 10 days.

Tarun's pay =10×2160== 10 \times 2160 = =10×2160= Rs 21,60021,60021,600

Varun's pay =7×2400== 7 \times 2400 = =7×2400= Rs 16,80016,80016,800

Total =21,600+16,800== 21,600 + 16,800 = =21,600+16,800= Rs 38,40038,40038,400

Note: Using Arun instead of Varun for the remaining 13\dfrac{1}{3}31​ work would require 1/31/24=8\dfrac{1/3}{1/24} = 81/241/3​=8 days, costing 8×2160=8 \times 2160 = 8×2160= Rs 17,28017,28017,280, which is more than Varun's Rs 16,80016,80016,800. Also, workers charge a full day's wage even for partial days, so only full days of work are optimal.

The minimum possible amount required is Rs 38,40038,40038,400.

questions.question_text: If a−6b+6c=4a - 6b + 6c = 4a−6b+6c=4 and 6a+3b−3c=506a + 3b - 3c = 506a+3b−3c=50, where aaa, bbb and ccc are real numbers, the value of 2a+3b−3c2a + 3b - 3c2a+3b−3c is
questions.explanation_text:

6[4+6(b−c)]+3(b−c)=506[4 + 6(b - c)] + 3(b - c) = 506[4+6(b−c)]+3(b−c)=50

24+36(b−c)+3(b−c)=5024 + 36(b - c) + 3(b - c) = 5024+36(b−c)+3(b−c)=50

39(b−c)=2639(b - c) = 2639(b−c)=26

b−c=2639=23b - c = \dfrac{26}{39} = \dfrac{2}{3}b−c=3926​=32​

Plug b−c=23b - c = \dfrac{2}{3}b−c=32​ back into Equation (3)(3)(3):

a=4+6×23=4+4=8a = 4 + 6 \times \dfrac{2}{3} = 4 + 4 = 8a=4+6×32​=4+4=8

2a+3b−3c=2a+3(b−c)2a + 3b - 3c = 2a + 3(b - c)2a+3b−3c=2a+3(b−c)

=2(8)+3 ⁣(23)= 2(8) + 3\!\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)=2(8)+3(32​)

questions.question_text: In a class, there were more than 10 boys and a certain number of girls. G=2B+403G = \dfrac{2B + 40}{3}G=32B+40​

Since the number of students must be whole numbers, and a "fraction of a student" cannot leave:

Also, B>10B > 10B>10 (given).

So possible values of BBB: 15,20,25,30,...15, 20, 25, 30, ...15,20,25,30,...

To find the minimum total, start with the smallest BBB:

For B=15B = 15B=15: G=2(15)+403=703=23.33G = \dfrac{2(15) + 40}{3} = \dfrac{70}{3} = 23.33G=32(15)+40​=370​=23.33 — not a whole number

For B=20B = 20B=20: G=2(20)+403=803=26.67G = \dfrac{2(20) + 40}{3} = \dfrac{80}{3} = 26.67G=32(20)+40​=380​=26.67 — not a whole number

For B=25B = 25B=25: G=2(25)+403=903=30G = \dfrac{2(25) + 40}{3} = \dfrac{90}{3} = 30G=32(25)+40​=390​=30 — whole number and a multiple of 555

Total students =B+G= B + G=B+G

=25+30= 25 + 30=25+30

=55= 55=55
